A situation concept that defines the upper limit of human capacity for high-quality decision-making under uncertainty. 
Encompasses: Cognitive load management, work duration limits, and performance degradation thresholds.

unmapped_concepts.concept: The document identifies a hard limit on human cognitive output, suggesting that high-quality judgment work is sustainable for only four to six hours per day. It frames this as a design constraint for any organization adopting AI, rather than a performance variable to be optimized away.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This concept is central to the document's argument for redesigning work and represents a specific constraint on AI-human integration.
unmapped_concepts.Accelerationist Interpretation: Accelerationists would view this as a design parameter to be optimized, potentially using AI to further reduce the cognitive load of judgment tasks or to augment human capacity to extend the duration of high-quality work.
unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: Safetyists would interpret this as a critical safety boundary, arguing that exceeding this limit creates systemic risk by increasing the likelihood of human error in high-stakes decision-making.
unmapped_concepts.Skeptic Interpretation: Skeptics would use this to argue against the 'AI makes work easier' narrative, highlighting that AI-driven work intensification is a direct threat to worker well-being and long-term cognitive health.
